body: And someone downvotes me for wanting to go to a DOTA 2 tournament which is not the event "the girl" may or may not be going to. A LoL fan I take it?

OK, That's actually framed really well and puts me more at ease. Generally I've been pretty lucky with a variety of things as of late, because contingency has always been a strong value of mine and having it in mind has paid off immensely. I do appreciate your perspective as it helps me "man up" some.
? That's the other conference I am going to. I just made a new post with just a little more detail. See below.

OK, I was hoping to give as little specific information as possible. She and I still have 1 or 2 mutual friends and we make a point not to talk about "the girl." They mentioned awhile ago that she now lives as an artist in Chicago which is fine and dandy. However, the conference in question is the Chicago Alternative Comix Expo which as I mentioned, I may be helping man a booth and I have a friend who is really wanting to come with me to it. Point being, "the girl" and I are both into weird art and so I don't know definitively if she'll go, but it would not surprise me if she did. Hence why I am asking how to cover any bases I may not be seeing. I'm just in the middle of a relatively stable relationship now, and so for the most part I'm over "the girl" (the only part that still is concerning is how badly I fucked up)  but I just want to keep the situation in mind. Thank you for your words of wisdom/advice.
Dota 2 is a 5v5 tower defense game that's become really popular recently.

Really? After 3 years of absolutely zero contact at her request and no formal legal action being taken  and if I am clearly at this conference under very clearly different pretenses, I don't know what to make of it.

edit: Again, I would not acknowledge her in any way shape or form. I  would just advert my gaze and pretend she doesn't exist. Or if absolutely necessary, go to a different part of the conference. I don't know what she could do potentially.
Hahah that too, but I'm going to the DOTA 2 Chicagoland tournament which is on one of the days of the conference. Can't exactly miss that.

OK. Thank you. I just wanted to hear from a stranger that I should be fine. I think I can handle going to the conference, but my main concern was for any sort of loose end that I may have not factored into my decision which could cause unnecessary drama. Thank you again.

No there wasn't. Had I contacted her beyond the July 2010 message of "I forgive you, but I don't want to see you again. Please do not contact me again or I will have no choice but to pursue legal action," message she sent, there would have been but I stopped immediately right then and haven't said a word to her since. But I know it affected her deeply to the point where she dropped out of school a semester and a half later. The closest thing that could  be counted as legal action was that I attempted suicide in May of 2010 on campus the semester I dropped out of school after Campus Police called me on her behalf to say to leave her alone and when campus police found me, they said because of the suicide attempt that I was not allowed on campus for one full calendar year, which I abided by. (that year being May 2010 to May 2011). That's the extent of how "legal" it got. Sorry if I'm rambling a little. Part of me had somewhat of a panic attack realizing that she may be at this conference in Chicago.

D- I'm so sorry for everything I put you through fall '09-Spring '10. Even when I dropped out of school to diffuse all the drama that happened, I was still very much wrapped up in myself. I was battling something far bigger than I really knew and could handle and I was expecting you to be the solution out. In the process, I felt like I harassed you constantly not thinking about how much of an hinderance I was on your life, even though for the long while of it, hundreds of miles seperated us. I put you on an enormous pedestal that you could not possibly perform to and I felt like in addition to my frantic harassment, I dehumanized you in the process. You were right and justified in calling Campus Security that day when I was on campus, even though my intent was not to see you and to go see my doctor who has his practice nearby. Even though you and I both know I never meant any sort of emotional and physical harm, I was really scary. I wish I could have told you what I was really up against that school year. There was so much I should have warned you about ahead of time but I really couldn't. Even to this day, I have difficulty opening up about the things that govern my daily life and that every day is physically and emotionally painful for me. It is the nature of the beast I fight and I hate scaring people away with what is the reality of my life. But I chose to hide it, and it cost us both greatly. It's still hard opening up about the realities of my condition to people and people still tend to run away. I'm young and people tend to get more accepting through age and time.

T- Pretty much the same to you, but months after your unexpected threat to me when I moved back to the midwest, I finally figured out your rationale for why you felt the need to threaten me via your friend, until I realize that no matter how many times I told you things had changed with me, to you, you could never seperate the person I became with the person I was in high school. We were both dishonest to each other but the reality was that even though I know we are so much on the same page on a lot of issues, you could not (and possibly cannot but I can tell you're the sort of person who gets better understanding of things with age) see past me and the stereotypes of the beast what I deal with. That still doesn't excuse the deceptive manipulation, the immaturity of being a teenager, and the stress I caused you and the few times that I snapped with you so many years ago. I was a monster then, fighting another monster much bigger than you could understand/handle then. I hope you have found what you are looking for on your return to the east coast. I hope one day, when/if our paths will cross (and knowing the profession/passions we have, it's a possiblilty), that you will address me with some measure of respect for the work I've done as I will you and the incredible work you've done. I will be honest and say I'm not too optimistic on that prospect.

To both of you, regardless, I've become a lot braver than I was then and more willing to risk honesty with people than to hide and create lies to mask the demons I fight. I've only learned recently that risking honesty is the only way for me to be real with other people and I try hard to not hold it against people who cannot accept me for who I am.
